A1.justification: Both complete PDFs, including their appendices, are readable and describe the same safety-neuron study. Methods, experiments and displays can be matched despite the changed title, structure and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three LLMs, including neuron patching, training-seed stability, alignment-tax interventions and safeguard classification.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Qwen2.5 experiments, evaluated localization baselines, general-capability benchmarks and joint-alignment analyses.

M1.justification: The activation-difference scoring, dynamic patching and logistic-regression detector remain unchanged; generation-time is renamed inference-time. A limited proposed inference extension appears in v2 Section 6: flagged prompts may continue with a refusal prefix, whereas v1 describes rejecting output. The reported safeguard evaluation still scores accepted responses.

E1.justification: v2 adds direct capability evaluation on MMLU, GSM8K, BBH and TruthfulQA, substantially extending v1's Wikitext-2 perplexity assessment to knowledge, mathematics, reasoning and truthfulness. The original red-teaming and preference-learning datasets remain. Appendix B.3 also documents circuit-breakers training data used for the SN-Tune baseline.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Pruning and SN-Tune localization baselines, called Param and Neuron in Table 8, beyond v1's random-neuron controls. Safeguard comparisons add unrestricted RN-All and remove the Majority classifier. Matched-layer and last-layer random controls remain under revised names.

E3.justification: v2 introduces normalized causal-effect evaluation, changes principal patching budgets from 20,000 neurons to 5%, and adds Qwen2.5-3B. Alignment-tax interventions select shared neurons using Safety/SHP rather than Harmless/Helpful. Safeguard evaluation changes from Beavertails-trained testing to averaging training-on-one/testing-on-pooled-others combinations. Appendix B.2 specifies new prompting, sampling and scoring protocols for the added capability benchmarks.

E4.justification: v2 adds causal comparisons across preference-neuron sets (Figure 3b) and a joint helpfulness/harmlessness training intervention (Appendix E.4, Table 10). Expanded safeguard sensitivity analysis tests whether layer distribution explains predictiveness. Existing model, prompt and token-position ablations remain, but their detailed cross-benchmark tables from v1 Tables 9–10 are omitted.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 2 reports confidence bands for random-neuron curves as well as safety-neuron curves. v1 Figure 2 lacked these bands, while Figure 3 reported intervals for safety neurons. Five training trials, 95% confidence intervals, five random draws for classifier comparisons and the t-test remain; no increased repetition count is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, Qwen2.5, capability and joint-training results and revises patched-model scores. For example, patched Llama2 Base's Beavertails cost changes from -7.2 in v1 Table 1 to -5.7 in v2 Table 8 under the revised neuron budget. Safeguard accuracy changes from 79.4% to 76.2% under different validation protocols, so this is not a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 4 introduces an explicit normalized causal-effect definition and explains its zero and unit reference values. The original activation-difference formula and component-preservation assumption remain. No theorem or proof is added; Equation 5 mainly formalizes the already-described (IA)3 implementation.

C1.justification: The central contributions—localizing safety neurons, explaining alignment tax and constructing a safeguard—remain. v2 adds a headline claim that ablation-selected neurons are ineffective in its verification setting and broadens capability-preservation language from general language modeling to general ability. These refine the contribution claims without replacing the central research thesis.

C2.justification: v2 extends the alignment-tax interpretation to competition during joint training, attributes some safeguard predictiveness to neuron layer distribution, and introduces Hydra-effect compensation as a possible weakness of ablation approaches. Appendix D.1 revises its explanation of the preferred model comparison. The principal limitations are retained and moved to Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 adds patching pseudocode, explicit (IA)3 implementation, Qwen2.5 dimensions, baseline-selection details and benchmark-specific evaluation instructions. Its abstract supplies a repository address described as available, replacing v1's promise of future release; availability was not externally verified. Existing core training hyperparameters, hardware and reported runtime remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially recasts related work around neuron-level interpretability and safety mechanisms, distinguishing representation engineering from mechanistic interpretability. It positions activation enhancement against pruning, ablation, attention-head and safety-layer approaches, adding substantive discussion of Wei, Zhao, Zhou, Li, Arditi and McGrath, among others. The earlier general preference-learning discussion is removed.

P1.justification: Beyond the new title and terminology, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction into a framework explanation and contribution bullets, separates Preliminaries from the introduction, integrates the former workflow discussion elsewhere, and rewrites related work. Limitations move to an appendix, and ethical considerations become a shorter Broader Impacts section.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, combines sparsity/stability and safeguard displays, and changes plot axes to neuron percentages and causal effects. Results are reorganized into a colored comparison table and expanded appendix table. Token projections are split between main text and appendix, and new alignment-tax displays are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens tests of the central claims through evaluated localization alternatives, capability assessments beyond perplexity, and additional causal alignment-tax controls. Expanded implementation and code-access information also improves reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of detailed safeguard and ablation tables. A material weakness remains: the abstract overstates capability preservation, since v2 Table 8 shows effects such as Mistral Base's GSM8K accuracy falling from 0.285 to 0.125 after patching.
